questions.question: Write short notes anyone of the following. a) Syrian Christians in Kerala b) Syrian colonization
questions.solution_html:
• Syrian chriatians in kerala
  • According to tradition, the Saint Thomas Christians were founded by Saint
  • Thomas the Apostle, one of Jesus' twelve apostles, in 52 ADSt. Thomas
  • preached the gospel in important centers of Kerala and established the churches
  • in Niranam, Quilon, Chayal, Kokkamangalam, Kottakkav, Kodungallore and
  • Palayoor. 1.Local traditions 2. Ancient writings 3. Rampan pattu 4. Margam
  • Kali pattu 5. Veeradiyan Pattu 6. The testimony of fathers of the Church 7.
  • Testimony of ancient liturgies 8. Existence of the tomb of St. Thomas at
  • Mylapore 9. Testimony of Historians
  • SYRIAN COLONIZATION’S
  • Immigration of Syrian Christians from Persia under Thomas of Cana:
  • The St. Thomas Christians of Malabar had trade connections with the Syrians of
  • Persia and Babylon. This relation became more intimate because of immigration
  • of Christians from Persia in the 4th Century.
  • The arrival of these colonists increased the prestige and strength of the
  • Malabar church. .It helped the Malabar church to carry on commercial relations
  • and trade with foreign countries like Egypt, Venice etc
  • It paved the way for the emergence of two sets of Christians in India
  • namely the ‘Thekkumbhagakkar’ and ‘Vadakkumbhagakar’.
  • Immigration of the Syrian Christians in the 9th Century. In
  • 825 A. D. a group of Christians from Persia reached Malabar under the leadership
  • of a merchant Sabariso.

questions.question: Write short notes on life and works of St. Ephrem.
questions.solution_html:
• LIFE AND WORKS OF ST. EPHREM
  • St. Ephrem is the greatest Syriac writer whose contributions are unique in the
  • fields of poetry, theology and Biblical interpretations. He is one of the most
  • prominent fathers and doctors of the universal Christian Church. He was born at
  • Nisibis in the Roman Empire about 306 AD. t. Ephrem grew as a brilliant
  • scholar and learned theologian. When St. Jacob went to Nicaea to take part in
  • the Ecumenical council of AD 325, Ephrem also accompanied him. Ephrem
  • played a significant role in refuting the heretical views of Arius in the council.
